Simon’s Calm Cues: what changes and what does not

How the current Simon game uses four labeled pads, twelve rounds, optional sound, and a Calm cues timing toggle without saving a durable best score.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Watch the pattern. Repeat it. No flashing required.

Play SimonBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: NoCharge Simon uses four labeled pads and a sequence that grows by one cue after each successful round. The Calm cues option lengthens the highlight and the gap between cues; it does not change the twelve-round goal.

Four named pads, one growing sequence

The pads are Ring, Wave, Peak, and Bloom. The first round has one cue. After a correct response, the next sequence adds one cue; the player repeats the full sequence in order. A wrong pad ends the run, and completing twelve rounds finishes it.

The game adds a cue using a seeded sequence. The sequence is generated in the page session; the game does not publish a leaderboard or save a best round to browser storage.

What Calm cues changes

Standard playback highlights each cue for 270 milliseconds, with a 150-millisecond gap. Calm cues uses a 430-millisecond highlight and a 260-millisecond gap. The option is disabled while the sequence is actively playing, so a setting change does not interrupt a cue sequence.

The live status names each pad and announces when it is the player’s turn. Sound is off until explicitly enabled. Labels and glyphs accompany the colored pads, so color and sound are not the only feedback channels.

What the counters mean

The page shows the current sequence length, input progress, and the highest round completed during the mounted page session. Resetting or replaying does not write that number to a local score key; reloading the page clears the component state.

Calm cues is a presentation choice, not a medical recommendation or a claim that every player will find the game comfortable. Use the current Simon page to inspect its controls and choose the pace that works for you.
